VoiceDraftAttribution.description:
The fixed attribution of every remotely stored Voice Draft.

All three fields are literals with defaults, so a producer can construct
the one valid value with no caller input and a consumer cannot mistake an
AI-authored draft for owner voice.

author.description: Always AI; owner authorship is inexpressible.
author.title: Author

voice_weight.description: Always zero; the draft never trains the owner's voice.
voice_weight.title: Voice Weight

WireTierCeiling.description:
The only two tier ceilings expressible on ``/v1``.

``/v1`` is remote by construction, and
:func:`creek_mcp.policy.admitted_ceiling` refuses any remote call declaring
a ceiling outside :data:`creek_mcp.policy.REMOTE_ADMITTED_CEILINGS` *before
dispatch*. Since #1073 that decision is transport-neutral, so every adapter
is meant to reach it the same way; the MCP surface does so today through
:meth:`creek_mcp.server._BoundedFastMCP.call_tool`, and #1074 mounts the
``/v1`` handlers that will. This enum mirrors that frozenset, so
``intimate`` and ``all`` are not merely refused at runtime — they cannot be
constructed at all, which is the half of the guarantee that does not depend
on a handler remembering to ask.

The same two values double as the wire's *tier* vocabulary (see
:class:`JournalUpsertRequest`, :class:`JournalUpsertResponse` and
:class:`ReflectionResponse`). The two vocabularies coincide by
construction: the set of tiers a remote caller may name is exactly the set
of ceilings a remote caller may declare, because a tier above the remote
cap is one no remote request can reach in either direction.

Attributes:
    OPEN: Openly publishable content only (ontology §13.2).
    PERSONAL: Adds personal — and, per #961, ``unclassified`` — content.
WireTierCeiling.title: WireTierCeiling

description:
The letter the vault wrote, and the Voice Draft now holding it.

Attributes:
    status: Always ``"ok"``. Failure is an :class:`ErrorEnvelope`, and an
        acute-distress entry is a :class:`CareEscalationResponse`.
    tier_ceiling: The caller's declared ceiling, echoed.
    external_id: The caller-owned id; ``DELETE
        /v1/voice-drafts/{external_id}`` retracts the letter.
    fragment_id: The stable vault-side fragment identity.
    action: ``created`` for a new letter, ``unchanged`` when the id already
        held one, which is returned as stored without a model call.
    tier: The stored letter's tier.
    title: The stored title.
    letter: The letter text. Free model prose, never a verbatim quote. A
        new letter is capped at :data:`MAX_LETTER_CHARS`; an ``unchanged``
        one is returned exactly as stored, so a draft put by
        ``PUT /v1/voice-drafts`` is never truncated on the way out.
    attribution: Fixed AI attribution and zero voice weight.
    inference_source: The route that answered, one of ``pool:creek``,
        ``pool:attested:<vendor>``, ``request_key:<vendor>`` or ``local``
        (ADR-0016 Decision 1 item 11). Since contract 0.19, and omitted
        for a caller declaring an earlier minor. Also omitted — rather
        than guessed — on an answer this vocabulary does not label, which
        today is an operator's own cloud key on a self-hosted vault or an
        attested enclave (unreadable, and still off-device). The
        consumer's use for the field is to notice a route it did not
        expect, so a label the server cannot stand behind would be worse
        than none.

action.description: Created, or unchanged when the id already held a letter.
action.title: Action

attribution.description: Fixed AI attribution and zero voice weight.

inference_source.description: Route that answered: pool:creek, pool:attested:<vendor>, request_key:<vendor> or local. Since contract 0.19.
inference_source.title: Inference Source

letter.description: The letter text; free model prose.
letter.title: Letter

status.description: Always ok; failure is an error.
status.title: Status
